request.text: What is the voltage on R1?

solution.item: *** Solution by TINA assisted by AI ***
At first we calculate the total resistance between the generator nodes (VS1)
R4 and R2 connected in series so Rd=R4+R2=1Ohm+1Ohm=2Ohm
R5 and Rd connected in parallel so Rc=R5*Rd/(R5+Rd)=2Ohm*2Ohm/(2Ohm+2Ohm)=1Ohm
Rc and R1 connected in series so Rb=Rc+R1=1Ohm+1Ohm=2Ohm
R3 and Rb connected in series so Ra=R3+Rb=1Ohm+2Ohm=3Ohm
Now we calculate the voltage on R1
We know that the voltage between VS1 nodes is 6V.
The components R3,Rb connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 6V.
Rb is in the voltage divider so the voltage on Rb is Rb/Ra*6V = 4V.
The components Rc,R1 connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 4V.
R1 is in the voltage divider so the voltage on R1 is R1/Rb*4V = 2V.
